newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sticks to 1997 tax cut plan - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Hungary sticks to 1997 tax cut plan - spokesman.

text.p: Hungary's government intends to maintain its income tax cut plans for 1997, a government official said on Thursday.

"The government has reaffirmed its plans to reduce the highest income tax bracket to 42 percent despite some members of parliament urging for a higher upper limit," government spokesman Elemer Kiss told a news conference, following the regular cabinet meeting.
The highest income tax bracket is currently 48 percent.
Kiss gave no further details, but earlier press reports had suggested some parlament members of the ruling Socialist Party wanted a 44-percent highest income tax bracket.
Kiss also said the government reaffirmed its intention to cut all income tax brackets, which would result in an overall lower tax burden for the population.
